Consider the vector field $F=⟨x-y,\,y+z,\,2x-3z⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by the bounding region of a right circular cylinder of height $3$ whose base is a circle of radius $2$ centered at the origin, as shown above. Given that $S$ is positively (outward) oriented, use the divergence theorem to find the flux of $F$ through $S.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x-y)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(y+z)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2x-3z) \\  & =1+1+(-3) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid cylinder enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}-1\,\text{d}V \\  & =-{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =-\text{Volume}(R) \\  & =-\pi \cdot {2}^{2}\cdot 3 \\  & =-12\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
